transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Reyes (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (Amberleaf Head of ML), Ethan Cole (Amberleaf Platform), Luis Ortega (Amberleaf Product)

Summary (auto): POC scoping to align on success criteria (latency, accuracy, hallucination), workload sizing, shortlist of open models for evaluation (tradeoffs for multilingual / financial domain), and a concrete 6-week bench + pilot timeline. Action items captured.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call — Jordan and I from Redwood. Who do we have on Amberleaf?
[00:06] Priya: Hi, Priya here — Head of ML. Ethan and Luis are with me.
[00:10] Ethan: Ethan, platform.
[00:12] Luis: Luis, product. Morning.
[00:14] Jordan (SE): Great. Goal for today is to size your workload, agree success criteria for the POC, and propose a focused model shortlist to run bench—should take about an hour.
[00:22] Priya: Sounds good. Quick context: Amberleaf builds event-driven financial insights — extraction of entities from earnings call transcripts, multilingual coverage in EN/ES/FR/PT, and a classification layer to tag risk signals. Our infra is AWS, VPC-only, and we need SSO + SOC2 evidence in parallel. Timeline ideally Nov->Dec POC with production decision in Jan.
[00:39] Maya: Got it. Two parallel constraints: security and latency/cost. Jordan, can you kick off with sizing questions?
[00:45] Jordan: Sure. Priya, what’s your expected QPS or daily tokens for the POC? Also typical sequence lengths?
[00:52] Priya: For the POC we'll simulate realistic load: ~200 concurrent users hitting async extract endpoints during market hours. Roughly 12k requests/day. Average sequence length pre-tokenization is around 1,800 tokens per request for full-call extraction, but we will also have a shorter 300-token summary endpoint. So mix: 70% long, 30% short.
[01:14] Jordan: Helpful. So ballpark we’re looking at ~ (12k * 0.7 * 1800) + (12k * 0.3 * 300) = ~15M tokens/day. For benching we'll do 1000 representative queries across both types to get latency/quality. Does that match your expectations?
[01:31] Priya: Yes, that aligns. Cost sensitivity — we want to see per-1M-token cost and also 95th percentile latency under 600ms for short requests and under 2s for long ones ideally.
[01:45] Luis: Product priority is accuracy for entity extraction — F1 > 0.88 on our labeled set, hallucination under 2% on identity fields, and consistent behavior across EN/ES/FR/PT.
[01:57] Maya: Perfect. Let's map that into measurable success criteria. Off the top: (1) Extraction F1 >=0.88, (2) hallucination rate <2% on PII, (3) short request p95 latency <=600ms, (4) cost per 1M tokens < $X (we'll model) and (5) deployment option validated (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC). Any additions?
[02:16] Priya: Also need audit logs and KMS integration for keys, that is must-have for success.
[02:20] Jordan: Noted. On models: we've prepped a shortlist focusing on open models and quantization-friendly families. Proposed models: Llama-2-Chat / Llama-3-lite (they said Llamer-3?), Mistral Turbo 7B, Mistral XL 11B, and a couple of Llama-2-70B-8bit variants. We also suggest trying a distilled multilingual model (we have a community-flavored polyglot 13B) for coverage.
[02:46] Priya: Quick note — we heard a lot about Llama-3 being good in reasoning, but suspect its multilingual robustness is mixed. We care a lot about Spanish and Portuguese.
[02:56] Jordan: Totally, that’s why we want to include a multilingual candidate. Also, we’ll test quantized versions (8-bit, Q4_0/Q4_K) to see tradeoffs: latency and memory vs accuracy drop.
[03:06] Ethan: For the private deployment, our infra team needs to know exact GPU footprints. Can you give a rough vGPU / RAM estimate per model?
[03:12] Jordan: Roughly — Mistral 7B quantized will run comfortably on a single A10 or t4-like vGPU with 24GB. Mistral XL / Llama-2 13B quantized 8-bit will need 1xA100-40GB or 2xA10 depending on batch; anything 70B likely requires 80GB+ or offload. We'll provide a sizing matrix. These are rough and depend on KV cache and sequence length.
[03:35] Luis: That's helpful. We may prefer smaller models if cost is a priority, but not at the expense of F1.
[03:42] Jordan: Right — that's the classic tradeoff. For extraction tasks often a well-tuned 13B can beat a naively-decoded 70B when latency constraints bite, especially with prefix-KV caching and prompt engineering.
[03:57] Priya: On benchmarks — what does Redwood typically run? Latency-only, quality-only, or combined?
[04:03] Maya: We do an integrated bench: (A) micro-latency/throughput tests (short and long sequences), (B) quality evals on your labeled set (entity F1, precision on PII), (C) hallucination/regression probes (structured checks), (D) cost simulation using your traffic profile. We'll share our bench harness and a spreadsheet.
[04:24] Priya: Good. For the labeled set, we have 2k annotated segments across 4 languages — we'll provide a stratified sample.
[04:32] Jordan: Perfect. For multilingual quality we recommend evaluating both zero-shot and few-shot (3-5 examples) per language; sometimes few-shot helps for less-resourced languages.
[04:43] Ethan: How long is the bench expected to take?
[04:45] Jordan: Initial run (quality + latency for 4 models) can be 3-5 days once we have datasets and access, then deeper throughput and cost analysis ~1 week. POC overall 4-6 weeks including integration and security review.
[04:57] Priya: Sounds doable. Security question — for Private (VPC) deployment, can Redwood support BYOK (bring your own key) and do you produce audit logs consumable by our SIEM?
[05:08] Maya: Yes — Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations (BYOK) and exports audit logs; we'll share the SOC2 and network docs. For Hosted we have encryption at rest and in transit but BYOK is a private-only feature.
[05:21] Luis: One more on evals — our product needs deterministic extraction for downstream automations. If models have intermittent omissions that's a dealbreaker. Do you do regression detection?
[05:31] Jordan: We run regression suites tied to the prompt set and labeled examples; Redwood Optimize can alert on quality regressions between model versions. For the POC we'll snapshot baseline and run nightly replays for a week.
[05:44] Priya: Okay. On model shortlist, can you list specific model files and quant levels we will test? We want the exact GitHub or hub names so we can audit licenses.
[05:53] Jordan: Sure — we'll include precise identifiers in the spreadsheet. Tentative shortlist: "mistral/latest-7b-q4", "mistral/xl-11b-8bit", "llama3-lite-13b-q4_k" (note: community name might vary), "polyglot-13b-multilang-q4" and a Llama-2-70b-8bit offload config for a high-water mark. We'll provide license summaries.
[06:20] Priya: Good. Any thoughts on few-shot prompt templates that reduce hallucination?
[06:25] Jordan: Yes — structured JSON prompt templates with clear field masks and examples help. We'll share a prompt engineering guide specialized for entity extraction to minimize hallucinations.
[06:33] Maya: Let’s talk acceptance criteria mapping to rollout options. If a model meets quality but costs too much, we can explore model-routing: short-calls to a faster small model, long-calls to a stronger model with async fallback. Redwood runtime can do smart routing and caching.
[06:48] Ethan: For routing, is that something we can configure at the app layer or does Redwood expose policies?
[06:53] Jordan: Exposed policies — you can set thresholds by latency, cost budget, or confidence score; automatic fallback to another model or cached response is supported.
[07:01] Priya: Confidence score — do you provide calibrated probabilities? We found raw token-level probs are noisy.
[07:06] Jordan: We provide calibration tooling and can compute confidence at the span/entity level via a small calibration head or ensemble checks. It's part of the evaluation.
[07:16] Luis: On timelines — can you outline a week-by-week POC plan?
[07:20] Maya: Sure, high level:
Week 0 (this week): Kickoff + data handoff + access setup (S3 share, VPC peering details)
Week 1: Baseline runs — 1k representative queries (latency + quality) across shortlist
Week 2: Deeper throughput runs, quantized variants, and cost modeling
Week 3: Multilingual few-shot tuning and hallucination probes
Week 4: Integration checks in Private VPC (if selected) + security review
Week 5: Final regression runs and acceptance testing on labeled set
Week 6: Wrap-up, decision, and production sizing docs
[07:53] Priya: That fits our target. SSO/SAML and audit logs need to be validated by Week 4.
[07:58] Maya: We'll add that to the checklist.
[08:00] Ethan: About infra access — for private benching, do you guys need full admin or can we create roles with limited permissions?
[08:07] Jordan: Limited roles are fine; we only need read access to sample buckets and temporary compute credentials if you want us to run on your infra. For Dedicated/Private we'll coordinate with your infra team for a secure deploy.
[08:18] Priya: One risk is tokenization differences across models (we saw entity boundaries shift). Will your bench normalize tokenization or report per-model token counts?
[08:28] Jordan: We'll report per-model tokenization stats and normalize metrics to entity-level F1 so differences in tokens don't skew the main quality metric.
[08:36] Luis: For evaluation metrics, we'll accept F1 + span exact match and a hallucination rate defined as any generated PII not present in source.
[08:45] Maya: Good — will formalize that definition in the bench doc.
[08:48] Priya: Pricing / cost modeling — can Redwood give estimates for hosted vs dedicated vs private at our expected scale?
[08:55] Maya: Yes. We'll run cost sims using your 15M tokens/day profile and produce per-1M-token numbers for each deployment option and model. For Dedicated we can show committed capacity pricing scenarios.
[09:06] Ethan: Any limitations around embeddings or reranking we should know? We'll likely use embeddings for semantic search over calls.
[09:12] Jordan: Embeddings are supported — we can evaluate both on semantic recall and cost. If you need private embeddings within VPC, that's supported in Private.
[09:21] Luis: One more — does Redwood keep training traces or data? We need assurance data won't be used to improve models unless we opt in.
[09:27] Maya: Redwood has explicit data handling controls; for Private and Dedicated we can guarantee no training use; Hosted has opt-in flags. We'll include specific language in the security doc.
[09:37] Priya: Great. Anything else on the model tradeoffs? I'm worried about 70B cost but we'd like to test it as an upper bound.
[09:44] Jordan: We'll include a 70B as a high-water mark. Expect improved zero-shot on some cases but diminishing returns for extraction tasks. The bench will measure marginal F1 improvement vs cost and latency so you can decide.
[09:57] Maya: Ok wrap-up recap: action items — Maya will send spreadsheet + bench harness by 11/12; Amberleaf will provide datasets and S3 access by 11/13; Jordan will run initial latency/throughput runs and share logs by 11/17. Redwood will include exact model identifiers and quant configs. Security docs and SOC2 will be shared.
[10:20] Priya: That timeline works. Quick Q: who owns the final acceptance test? Priya: We'll own acceptance but Redwood will help run the bench.
[10:27] Maya: Noted. We'll be in close touch.
[10:30] Ethan: Any blockers on our side? We'll prepare an IAM role and sanitized data.
[10:34] Jordan: Perfect. We'll also prepare a short runbook for the bench to make it frictionless.
[10:39] Luis: Thanks — pretty aligned.
[10:41] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with invites for the bench kick next Tuesday and share docs.
[10:47] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[10:49] End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings: "Llamer-3" instead of Llama-3, "A10" sometimes transcribed as "a ten"; names spelled phonetically. Timestamps approximate every 20-90 seconds.

- PII hallucination rate < 2%
- Short request p95 latency <= 600ms; long request p95 <= 2s
- Deployment option validated (Private/VPC prep or Dedicated)
- Security docs and KMS/BYOK validated

POC timeline (recap): 6-week scoped POC with bench + integration + security validation.
